attributes.morphology: equiaxed or near-equiaxed primary TiC; short rod eutectic TiC

evidence.quote: In TMC2, primary TiC exhibits equiaxed or near-equiaxed shape with sizes mainly in the range from 5 µm to 10 µm, while eutectic TiC shows short rod shape, as shown in Fig. 1(b). Primary TiC accounts for the majority of the reinforcements.
TiC grows in long strip shape in TMC1 (Fig. 1a), which is eutectic TiC.

attributes.size: slightly larger than those in TMC2

evidence.quote: A large proportional of primary TiC particles in TMC3 still display equiaxed or near-equiaxed shape and their sizes are slightly larger than those in TMC2 (Fig. 1c). In addition, some primary TiC exhibits dendritic characteristic.
reinforcements are uniformly distributed in the matrix macroscopically.

attributes.morphology: cleavage planes and tearing ridges or dimples

evidence.quote: The fracture surfaces of TMC2 and TMC3 are composed of the cleavage planes and tearing ridges or dimples (Fig. 5b and c), indicating a mixed ductile and brittle fracture mode at 700 ◦C.

As tensile temperature increases to 800 ◦C, fracture surfaces of all composites show dimple characteristic (Fig. 5a–f), showing that the composites all fractured in a ductile manner and void nucleation, growth and coalescence cause the fracture of TMC1, TMC2 and TMC3.
the UTS of TMC1 at 800 ◦C is 244.1 ± 4.2 MPa, reduced significantly compared to the as-cast UTS (Table 1).

Load-bearing effect of TiC with long strip shape is more evident than that with equiaxed morphology, resulting in the marginal discrepancy in the ultimate tensile strengths of the composites with 5 and 10 vol.% TiC.
the strengthening effect of C is mainly attributed to two factors: one is the solid solution of C in matrix; the other is load-bearing mechanism of TiC particles
the enhanced strength of matrix due to an improvement in the dislocation density of matrix is a more important strengthening effect

matrix softening is more and more serious with increasing test temperature. The fracture surfaces of TMC2 and TMC3 are composed of the cleavage planes and tearing ridges or dimples (Fig. 5b and c), indicating a mixed ductile and brittle fracture mode at 700 ◦C.

As tensile temperature increases to 800 ◦C, fracture surfaces of all composites show dimple characteristic (Fig. 5a–f), showing that the composites all fractured in a ductile manner and void nucleation, growth and coalescence cause the fracture of TMC1, TMC2 and TMC3.

Load-bearing effect of TiC with long strip shape is more evident than that with equiaxed morphology, resulting in the marginal discrepancy in the ultimate tensile strengths of the composites with 5 and 10 vol.% TiC.
